When a child can start

Parents often ask at what age a child can try Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ or Compak® Sporting. There is no single answer: the minimum age is set by the country's law, the ground's rules and its insurance. Many clubs start children at around 10–12; this is club practice, not a rule, so check local law and ask the club first.

Under the FITASC category table valid from 1 January 2027, boys and girls are in the Junior category from 1 January of the year they turn 13 until the end of the year they turn 20. This is a competition category, not a minimum age for starting to shoot.

The age on paper matters less than readiness. Can the child hold a gun steadily? Do they listen carefully and follow an adult's commands each time? Can they stay focused for a whole short session? If a child is easily distracted or treats a gun like a toy, it is better to wait a few months.

The first sessions are run only by a qualified coach or instructor, if possible one to one. The coach explains the safety rules, checks which eye leads (the master eye) and decides when the first shot can be fired. Parents do not replace the coach, even if they shoot well themselves.

A child usually starts with a light gun, often a 20 gauge; the bigger the gauge number, the narrower the barrel. Many makers offer a youth gun with a shorter stock. Pair it with soft low-recoil cartridges, for example 21–24 g of shot. A very light gun with a heavy load can still kick hard, so the load matters as much as the gauge. The aim is that the shot neither frightens nor hurts. Fitting a gun to a child: Equipment that fits a child.

The first targets should be simple and slow, for example a target flying straight away from the shooter (a going-away target). A session has few shots and ends on a good one, so that the child leaves the ground smiling.

Safety: A child needs safety glasses and hearing protection that fit a small head, from the very first shot. Adult ear muffs can sit loosely on a child; check the fit before shooting starts. More: Eye and ear protection.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

At Sporting™ competitions the rules also require children on the range, outside the clubhouse, to wear hearing protection.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 8 · Hearing protection is compulsory

Before the first visit, call the ground and ask: from what age do they take children? Is there a junior programme, a coach for children and a 20 gauge gun to hire? The answers tell you quickly whether the club suits you.

Key points

  • The minimum age is set by the country's law and the club's rules: check them.
  • The child's readiness matters more than age.
  • Start only with a coach, if possible one to one.
  • A light gun, often 20 gauge, with soft cartridges; glasses and ear protection that fit.
  • Simple targets, few shots, finish on a good shot.

Did you know?

Gauge is historically defined by how many equal lead balls the size of the bore (the inside of the barrel) can be made from one English pound of lead. That is why a 20 gauge has a narrower bore than a 12.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Who sets the minimum age at which a child may shoot?

    1. National law and the ground's rules
    2. The parents alone, as they wish
    3. The company that made the gun
    Answer

    National law and the ground's rules

    The age depends on the country's law, the club's rules and its insurance, so check them first.

  2. What gun is a child often given in the first sessions?

    1. A heavy 12 gauge with long barrels
    2. A light 20 gauge with soft cartridges
    3. Any gun the family has at home
    Answer

    A light 20 gauge with soft cartridges

    A 20 gauge suits a smaller body and is fired with light cartridges; it is the light cartridge, not the light gun, that makes the recoil softer.

  3. How should a child's first session end?

    1. With the hardest target of the day
    2. When the box of cartridges is empty
    3. On a good shot, before the child tires
    Answer

    On a good shot, before the child tires

    Ending on a success leaves a good memory and the wish to come back.
